runs.summary: 4 new podcast recommendations for week of 2026-10-29 (The Missing Cryptoqueen, Rational Reminder, The Children's Book Podcast, The Value Perspective)
runs.content:
## Week of 2026-10-29

### The Missing Cryptoqueen (BBC Sounds)
Host: Jamie Bartlett (producer Georgia Catt)
Why for Fred: Fred went straight through Off Duty, Where Is Austin Tice? and podcast cyberhack the conti files bbc episode 6, so serialised BBC investigations clearly suit him. This one covers crypto, his DeFi interest. It is the story of OneCoin, a "Bitcoin killer" that raised billions and turned out to have no blockchain, and of its founder Ruja Ignatova, who disappeared in 2017. It shows how a crypto fraud works: MLM-style distribution, fake on-chain claims, laundering. That is useful pattern-recognition for judging DeFi protocols. A January 2026 teaser announced four new episodes, so the story is live again.
Format: Serialised narrative documentary, ~14 episodes so far, ~30–40 min each
Sample episode to start with: Episode 1. Start at the beginning; the 2022 follow-ups ("The Dubai Files", "Operation Satellite") and the 2026 episodes continue the hunt.
Links: BBC Sounds (search "The Missing Cryptoqueen") · Jamie Bartlett's Substack note (https://jamiejbartlett.substack.com/p/the-missing-cryptoqueen) · TuneIn (https://tunein.com/podcasts/The-Missing-Cryptoqueen-p1256038)

---

### The Rational Reminder Podcast
Hosts: Ben Felix, Cameron Passmore (PWL Capital, now part of OneDigital)
Why for Fred: This is the evidence-based counterweight to Fred's stock-picking diet (Behind the Balance Sheet, Pender, Dividend Talk). Felix and Passmore interview academics such as Eugene Fama, Ken French and Michael Kitces on factor premia, behavioural biases, what the data says about dividends and value, and decision-making. That touches his behavioural-economics interest and the wiki's factor investing page directly. It is also a useful stress test for his dividend-tilted portfolio: they are well-known sceptics of "dividend investing" as a factor.
Format: Long-form interview / discussion, weekly, ~60–90 min
Sample episode to start with: Any guest episode with Eugene Fama or Ken French, or a "dividends" episode. For the show's own back story, Ep 389, "How the Rational Reminder Podcast is Made" (Dec 25, 2025).
Links: rationalreminder.ca (https://rationalreminder.ca) · PWL Capital (https://pwlcapital.com/?p=17151)

---

### The Children's Book Podcast
Host: Matthew C. Winner (school librarian; formerly "All The Wonders", running since 2013)
Why for Fred: This is the first craft pick aimed at Lightfin. Winner interviews children's authors and illustrators about how a story gets from idea to finished book: voice, rhythm, what makes young listeners lean in. That transfers directly to writing children's audio stories. It's warm and conversational, with 850+ episodes and new ones still coming out in 2026. Previous creative picks (Scriptnotes, Writing Excuses, Creative Penn, Circle Round) were about adult craft, publishing, or finished kids' audio, not the children's-author craft itself.
Format: Interview, weekly, ~30–45 min
Sample episode to start with: "A Muppets Sensibility with John Patrick Green" (Jul 2026), on humour for kids. Or Andy Griffiths (May 2026), master of read-aloud comic storytelling.
Links: Podcast Addict (https://podcastaddict.com/podcast/6634261) · Podscan (https://podscan.fm/podcasts/the-childrens-book-podcast)

---

### The Value Perspective (Schroders)
Hosts: Juan Torres Rodriguez (co-manager, Schroders EM Value) with Andy Evans; earlier episodes Andrew Lyddon / Kevin Murphy
Why for Fred: It's made by Schroders' London value team, which makes it one of the few European value-investing podcasts run by practitioners. Long interviews with fund managers (Nick Train, Jonathan Boyar, Rob Gardner, Adam Rozencwajg) and author William Green on behaviour, cycles and patience fit his MOI/Berkshire principles. There's a nice cross-link: Tobias Carlisle hosted Juan in a "meet the manager" episode, and Fred has just heard Carlisle on Behind the Balance Sheet. Caveat: I couldn't confirm any episode after Aug 2025, so treat it as a strong back catalogue (~200 episodes) rather than a live weekly.
Format: Long-form interview, roughly weekly while active, ~40–60 min
Sample episode to start with: "The Value Perspective with Nick Train", or the London Value Investor Conference '25 specials (June 2025)
Links: schroderstvp.podbean.com (https://schroderstvp.podbean.com) · Schroders LVIC '25 episode (https://www.schroders.com/en-gb/uk/intermediary/insights/the-value-perspective-podcast-at-the-london-value-investor-conference-25/)

---

runs.content:
## Week of 2026-10-22

### In Good Company with Nicolai Tangen
Host: Nicolai Tangen (CEO, Norges Bank Investment Management; ex-AKO Capital)
Why for Fred: Tangen, a former European hedge-fund founder, interviews the CEOs of the companies Norway's sovereign fund owns (Aviva, Orange, Arista), plus macro and geopolitics figures (Georgieva, Stoltenberg). It's a European-investor take on management quality, next to Behind the Balance Sheet.
Format: Weekly long-form CEO interview (~45-60 min) + Friday highlights
Start with: Michael Bloomberg (2026), or Amanda Blanc on the Aviva turnaround
Links: https://www.nbim.no/en/news-and-insights/podcast/

### ChinaTalk
Host: Jordan Schneider
Why for Fred: Where AI meets geopolitics: chips, export controls, GPU smuggling, China's AI labs. It's the policy layer under the Dwarkesh compute-economics episodes and the world-order themes from the Prof. Jiang episode. Guests are specialists, not pundits.
Format: Long-form interview/panel, several a week, ~45-90 min
Start with: "GPU Smuggling, OpenAI Cooked?" with Nathan Lambert (Mar 2026)
Links: https://www.chinatalk.media

### The Lazarus Heist (BBC World Service)
Hosts: Geoff White, Jean Lee
Why for Fred: The natural next listen after CyberHack: The Conti Files and Where Is Austin Tice?. A serialised BBC investigation of North Korea's state hackers, from the $1bn Bangladesh Bank attempt to crypto-exchange thefts. Peabody-nominated, and it links to his DeFi interest.
Format: Serialised documentary, multiple seasons, ~30 min episodes
Start with: Season 1, Episode 1
Links: BBC Sounds
